How I see design

Find the signal.
Lose the noise.

I connect user needs, business goals, and the effort it takes to build. My aim is to find the smallest useful change that makes a meaningful difference.

At Hamrah Mechanic, I worked as a Product Designer and Associate Product Manager at the same time. That experience taught me to question what we should build, weigh trade-offs, and connect design decisions to product outcomes.

I bring that perspective into discovery: understand the problem, choose where to focus, and define what success looks like.

My approach, in a small interaction.

Before the job title · Tehran, 2020

My first design studio
was a night shift.

Before I was a designer, I was a night security guard.

In 2020, I worked at Almas Tower, a residential building in Tehran. I was dealing with the demands of that job while trying to build a different future for myself. Design began in the time I could find between those responsibilities.

During the quiet hours, I practiced and read books about design and business. There was no design title yet—just work, learning, and the decision to keep going. Progress came a little at a time.

Later that year, I started working in UI and UX design at IMPC. From there, I moved into automotive products, travel, restaurant operations, and grocery shopping. Each step gave me new problems to understand.

That beginning still shapes how I work. I know what it means to work with limited resources. I look for practical ways forward, stay close to people’s real circumstances, and keep learning when the answer isn’t obvious.
